title: Defining A₅ and Computing Its Order
content: The alternating group A₅ = ker(sign : S₅ → ℤ/2) has |A₅| = 5!/2 = 60. This is verified by native_decide, which exhaustively enumerates the even permutations of Fin 5.
mathContext: A₅ = alternatingGroup(Fin 5) is the kernel of the sign homomorphism sgn : S₅ → {±1}. Since S₅ has order 5! = 120 and sgn is surjective, |A₅| = 120/2 = 60 = 2²·3·5.
significance: The factorization 60 = 2²·3·5 determines exactly which primes require Sylow analysis and what constraints Sylow III will impose. The 2-adic valuation 2 (not 1) means Sylow 2-subgroups have order 4, not 2, making the counting more constrained.

title: Sylow III Constrains All Three Primes
content: Sylow III gives two constraints for each prime p dividing 60: n_p ≡ 1 (mod p) and n_p divides the index [A₅ : P_p]. These are Mathlib's card_sylow_modEq_one and card_sylow_dvd_index applied to A₅.
mathContext: For p=2: n₂ ≡ 1 (mod 2) and n₂ | 15, so n₂ ∈ {1, 3, 5, 15}. For p=3: n₃ ≡ 1 (mod 3) and n₃ | 20, so n₃ ∈ {1, 4, 10}. For p=5: n₅ ≡ 1 (mod 5) and n₅ | 12, so n₅ ∈ {1, 6}. The exact values (5, 10, 6) are determined by native_decide in the next section.
significance: The divisibility constraint n_p | [G:P_p] combined with the congruence n_p ≡ 1 (mod p) dramatically restricts the possible values. For n₅, only {1, 6} are allowed — and since A₅ is non-abelian simple (a fact we're proving), n₅ = 6.

title: Exact Sylow Numbers via native_decide
content: The exact Sylow numbers n₂ = 5, n₃ = 10, n₅ = 6 are computed by native_decide, which exhaustively enumerates all Sylow p-subgroups of A₅. The 5 Sylow 2-subgroups are Klein 4-groups V₄ ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/2; the 10 Sylow 3-subgroups are cyclic ⟨(ijk)⟩; the 6 Sylow 5-subgroups are cyclic ⟨(ijklm)⟩.
mathContext: native_decide evaluates Fintype.card (Sylow p A5) by computing the number of Sylow p-subgroups as a Fintype. This requires the Fintype instance for Sylow p G, which Mathlib provides via the orbit-stabilizer theorem.
significance: All three exact values exceed 1, immediately implying (via the uniqueness criterion) that no Sylow p-subgroup is normal — a key step toward proving simplicity. The values also match the theoretical lower bounds from the congruence/divisibility constraints.
prerequisites: Sylow III constraints from previous section

title: No Sylow Subgroup is Normal: Clean Contradiction
content: The proof of non-normality uses a clean contradiction: if a Sylow p-subgroup P were normal, Sylow.unique_of_normal would give Unique (Sylow p A5), forcing Fintype.card = 1. But we computed n₂ = 5, n₃ = 10, n₅ = 6 — contradiction.
mathContext: The key Mathlib lemma is Sylow.unique_of_normal: a normal Sylow p-subgroup is the unique Sylow p-subgroup (all conjugates of a normal subgroup equal itself). Uniqueness then forces Fintype.card (Sylow p G) = 1 via Fintype.card_unique.
significance: This argument works uniformly for all three primes. The logical structure — assume normality, derive uniqueness, contradict the computed count — is the standard proof template for showing no Sylow subgroup is normal.

title: Conjugacy Class Arithmetic via decide
content: The conjugacy class size theorem is proved by decide (kernel computation over Bool⁴): for each subset selection (a,b,c,d) ∈ Bool⁴ choosing from {12, 12, 15, 20}, the sum 1 + selected either equals 1, 60, or doesn't divide 60.
mathContext: The conjugacy classes of A₅ have sizes {1, 12, 12, 15, 20} with sum 60. A normal subgroup is a union of conjugacy classes containing the identity, so its order is 1 plus a subset-sum from {12, 12, 15, 20}. The `decide` tactic exhaustively checks all 16 = 2⁴ cases.
significance: This theorem provides the second half of the simplicity proof: not only are there no normal Sylow subgroups (from counting), but no subgroup of intermediate order can exist (from conjugacy class arithmetic). The `decide` proof is a machine-verified exhaustive check.
relatedConcepts: normal subgroup as union of classes

title: A₅ is Simple: Mathlib's Definitive Result
content: Mathlib's alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five provides the definitive simplicity result. The Sylow counting and conjugacy class analysis above give the concrete arithmetic reason why A₅ is simple.
mathContext: IsSimpleGroup G states that G has exactly two normal subgroups: ⊥ (trivial) and ⊤ (the whole group). Mathlib proves this for all alternating groups Aₙ with n ≥ 5 via alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five, which encapsulates the full proof.
significance: A₅ ≅ PSL(2,5) is the smallest non-abelian simple group. Its simplicity is the obstruction to solving the general degree-5 polynomial by radicals (Abel-Ruffini theorem): S₅ is not solvable because A₅ is its non-solvable composition factor.
prerequisites: normal subgroup analysis from previous sections

title: A₅ Not Solvable: Key to Abel-Ruffini
content: Non-solvability transfers from A₅ to S₅: if A₅ were solvable, then S₅ ≅ A₅ ⋊ ℤ/2 would be solvable (as an extension of solvable groups). This contradicts Mathlib's Equiv.Perm.not_solvable for n ≥ 5. This is the key ingredient for Abel-Ruffini.
mathContext: The proof uses solvable_of_ker_le_range: the kernel of sgn : S₅ → ℤ/2 is contained in the image of A₅ ↪ S₅. If A₅ were solvable, S₅ would be solvable (extension of solvable groups) — contradicting Equiv.Perm.not_solvable for n ≥ 5. The solvability criterion: G is solvable iff its derived series G ⊇ [G,G] ⊇ [[G,G],[G,G]] ⊇ ... terminates at {e}. Simple non-abelian A₅ has [A₅,A₅] = A₅, so the series never terminates.
significance: The chain A₅ simple → A₅ not solvable → S₅ not solvable → degree-5 polynomials not generally solvable by radicals is the heart of Galois theory. This theorem formalizes the group-theoretic obstruction.
prerequisites: short exact sequence A₅ → S₅ → ℤ/2
